usage: Pocari Sweat (포카리스웨트), Powerade (파워에이드) are the typical brands
When you sweat, a sports drink is good
common advice after exercise or when sick
For a hangover it's gotta be a sports drink
very common hangover remedy talk; -지 adds a knowing tone
examples: I drank a sports drink after working out.
몸살 났을 때 물보다 이온음료가 더 나아요.
When you have body aches, a sports drink is better than water.
Koreans often reach for these when sick
편의점에서 이온음료 한 병 사 왔어.
I grabbed a bottle of sports drink from the convenience store.
nuance: 이온음료 literally means 'ion drink' and refers to electrolyte sports drinks like 포카리스웨트. Koreans drink it not just for sports but routinely for hangovers and when feeling under the weather, where an English speaker might just say 'Gatorade'. It is sold in nearly every convenience store cooler.
mistakes: Don't confuse it with 에너지음료 (energy drink like Red Bull/핫식스) — 이온음료 has no caffeine kick, it's for hydration.
It's one word: 이온음료, not 이온 음료수.

usage: made from 매실 (Korean green plum) syrup; sweet-and-sour
many traditional cafes serve it hot or iced
소화 안 될 때 매실차 마셔
Drink plum tea when your digestion is off
매실 is a folk remedy for upset stomach
Plum tea is sweet and sour
examples: My stomach was upset so I drank plum tea.
This restaurant serves plum tea as a dessert drink.
In summer I make plum tea cold (with the syrup).
nuance: 매실차 is made by diluting 매실청 (plum syrup) with water, hot or cold. Beyond being a tasty drink, it has a strong reputation as a digestive aid, so a host may offer it after a heavy meal. You'll see it on the menu at traditional teahouses (전통찻집) and Korean restaurants.
mistakes: 매실 alone is the fruit (green plum); the drink is 매실차.
Don't expect a tea bag — it's syrup diluted in water, so it's sweet, not a steeped herbal tea.

usage: made from 유자 marmalade stirred into hot water
감기 기운 있을 때 유자차 마셔요
Drink citron tea when you feel a cold coming on
loaded with vitamin C; classic cold remedy
Citron tea is good for a sore throat
examples: My throat was scratchy so I made some citron tea.
In winter, warm citron tea is the best.
마트에서 유자청 사면 집에서 유자차 만들 수 있어요.
If you buy citron marmalade at the mart, you can make citron tea at home.
nuance: 유자차 is a thick, sweet hot drink made by spooning 유자청 (citron marmalade) into hot water. It's a go-to comfort drink in winter and a folk remedy for colds and sore throats. A jar of 유자청 in the fridge is extremely common in Korean homes.
mistakes: It's a marmalade-based drink, not a steeped tea — you'll find chunks of citron peel in the cup.
The headword is one word: 유자차, not 유자 차 with a space.

usage: fizzy fruit drink at cafes: 레몬에이드, 자몽에이드, 청포도에이드
I'll have an ade instead of coffee
examples: It was hot so I ordered a cold lemon ade.
The green-grape ade here is really good.
When I go to a cafe, I only drink ade.
for people who don't drink coffee
nuance: 에이드 (from English '-ade') is the standard cafe word for a sparkling fruit drink, almost always served iced with syrup and carbonated water. It's the most popular non-coffee, non-tea option, so if you don't drink coffee, ordering an 에이드 is the natural move. Flavors are named with the fruit + 에이드.
mistakes: Pronounced/written 에이드, not 에이드음료 or 에이드주스.
It's carbonated — if you want a non-fizzy fruit drink, that's 주스 (juice), not 에이드.

usage: blended icy fruit drink at cafes
A smoothie and a frappuccino are different
examples: 과일 스무디 한 잔이면 아침 대신 돼요.
One fruit smoothie works as a breakfast replacement.
대신 되다 = works as a substitute
The mango smoothie is the most popular here.
The smoothie was so cold it gave me brain freeze.
머리가 띵하다 = head goes numb/brain freeze
nuance: 스무디 is a blended, slushy fruit drink and a common healthier-feeling cafe order. The fruit name usually comes before it (딸기 스무디, 망고 스무디), and it can be written with or without a space. It's distinct from a milkshake (셰이크) and from coffee-based blended drinks.
mistakes: Don't call a coffee blended drink a 스무디 — coffee ones are 프라푸치노/블렌디드.
스무디 is the fixed spelling; avoid 스무디스 even though the chain is named that way.

usage: milky, lightly fizzy fermented rice alcohol, ~6%
On rainy days it's makgeolli with green-onion pancake
it settles, so you shake it first
examples: 전 부치는 날엔 꼭 막걸리를 마셔요.
On days we make jeon (pancakes), we always drink makgeolli.
This makgeolli isn't sweet and tastes clean.
막걸리를 너무 많이 마시면 머리가 아파요.
If you drink too much makgeolli, you get a headache.
nuance: 막걸리 is a milky, slightly sparkling rice alcohol around 6%, traditionally drunk from a bowl (사발) and famously paired with 파전 (green-onion pancake) on rainy days. It separates in the bottle, so you shake or stir it before pouring. It feels casual and homey compared to 소주 or 맥주.
mistakes: It's lightly carbonated and settles — shake it, or you'll pour cloudy sludge at the end.
Don't translate it as 'rice beer'; the standard English is 'makgeolli' or 'rice wine'.

usage: the base for the now-trendy 하이볼
한 잔 = one glass; offering a drink
I drink whiskey on the rocks
얼음에 = with ice / on the rocks
Whiskey bars are popular these days
위스키 바 = whiskey bar, a recent trend
examples: Whiskey is strong so I drink it little by little.
If you mix whiskey with sparkling water, it becomes a highball.
I got a bottle of whiskey as a gift.
nuance: 위스키 has surged in popularity in Korea recently, driven by the 하이볼 boom and a wave of dedicated whiskey bars. People drink it neat, on the rocks, or mixed into a highball. Calling it 독하다 (strong) is the natural way to describe its high alcohol content.
mistakes: Spelling is 위스키, not 위스키주 or 위스끼.
Don't say 위스키 술 — 위스키 already means the liquor.

usage: espresso + water; by far the most ordered cafe drink in Korea
아이스 아메리카노 = iced americano, the national default
the question you'll be asked when ordering coffee
아아 = 아이스 아메리카노; 뜨아 = 뜨거운 아메리카노
examples: I drink an americano every morning.
I drink only iced americanos even in winter.
'얼어 죽어도 아이스' is a real cultural meme
nuance: 아메리카노 is the overwhelming default coffee order in Korea, especially 아이스 아메리카노 (iced), which many drink year-round — hence the joke 얼어 죽어도 아이스 ('iced even if I freeze to death'). Knowing the slang 아아 (iced) and 뜨아 (hot) will make you sound like a local. Expect the barista to ask 따뜻한 거요, 아이스요?
mistakes: Don't ask for just 'coffee' (커피) at a cafe — they'll need a specific drink; 아메리카노 is the safe default.
아아 means iced americano specifically, not any iced coffee.

usage: often shortened to 생맥; sold by 잔 (glass) or 피처 (pitcher)
오백 = 500cc glass; 천 = 1000cc; counting by 개 is common
Shall we order a pitcher of draft?
examples: With fried chicken, cold draft beer is the best.
After work we went for a draft beer.
한잔하다 = to go for a drink
The draft here is cheaper than bottled beer.
병맥주 = bottled beer, the contrast term
nuance: 생맥주 (literally 'fresh/raw beer') is draft beer and a staple of Korean drinking spots, especially with fried chicken (치맥). It's ordered by glass size — 오백 (500cc) and 천 (1000cc) — and pitchers (피처) for groups. The clipped form 생맥 is very common in speech.
mistakes: 생맥주 is draft (on tap); bottled beer is 병맥주, canned is 캔맥주 — don't mix them up.
When ordering by size say 오백/천, not '500밀리리터'.

usage: whiskey + sparkling water + ice; hugely trendy right now
standard order at a bar or izakaya
A highball is low-proof so it's easy to drink
examples: 요즘 회식 때 하이볼 많이 마셔요.
These days we drink a lot of highballs at company dinners.
하이볼 has partly replaced 소주 for many
They sell canned highballs even at convenience stores.
Highballs are smoother than soju, so I like them.
nuance: 하이볼 is whiskey topped with sparkling water over ice, and it has become one of the trendiest drinks in Korea, popular at izakayas (이자카야), bars, and even as canned convenience-store versions. Because it's lower-proof and refreshing, many younger drinkers now choose it over 소주. Flavored versions like 레몬 하이볼 are everywhere.
mistakes: A highball is whiskey-based; it's not the same as an 에이드 (non-alcoholic fruit soda).
Don't pronounce it 하이볼을 as 'high-ball-uh' awkwardly — it's a fully naturalized loanword.

usage: for coffee, tea, broth, milk — concentrated flavor
진하게 = strongly; asking for an extra shot feel
examples: 이 녹차는 너무 진해서 좀 써요.
This green tea is so strong it's a bit bitter.
If you add less milk, it gets stronger.
nuance: 진하다 describes a deep, concentrated flavor — strong coffee, dark tea, rich broth, or creamy milk. For coffee it's the natural word for 'strong' (not 강하다). Its opposite is 연하다 (weak/light). Use 진하게 when asking a barista to make a drink stronger.
mistakes: For a strong-tasting drink use 진하다, not 강하다 (강하다 is more for force/intensity in general).
For high-alcohol liquor, the word is 독하다, not 진하다 — 진하다 is about flavor concentration, not proof.

usage: neither hot nor cold; often a complaint about a drink
useful when you don't want it cold (e.g. taking medicine)
examples: The beer is lukewarm so it tastes bad.
Take the medicine with lukewarm water.
The americano had cooled off and was lukewarm.
nuance: 미지근하다 means lukewarm/tepid — a drink that's lost its heat or never got cold. It often carries a mildly negative nuance (a beer or coffee that should be hot or cold but isn't). It's also genuinely useful for requesting 미지근한 물, which people prefer for taking medicine or for sensitive stomachs.
mistakes: 미지근하다 = lukewarm; 따뜻하다 = pleasantly warm. A lukewarm drink that should be hot is 미지근하다 (a complaint), not 따뜻하다.
Don't use it for weather; it's mainly for liquids and objects, not air temperature (that's 포근하다/따뜻하다).
